disease_label_per_paper: Hepatitis C-induced mixed cryoglobulinemia complicated by severe cutaneous vasculitis with ischemic limbs
presentation_summary: 55-year-old man with treatment-naive genotype 1a HCV presented with bilateral hand pain and diffuse purpuric rash.
He reported arthralgias, purpuric lesions, weakness, and numbness.
Physical examination showed palpable purpura and extensive gangrene involving both upper and lower extremities.
Laboratory evaluation showed RF >1200 IU/mL, C4 <8.0 mg/dL, HCV RNA 2390000 IU/mL, and positive cryoglobulins.
Leg skin biopsy showed acute inflammatory infiltrate and small to mid-sized vessels with fibrin thrombi with or without associated vasculitis.

Despite plasmapheresis, pulse steroids, prednisone, rituximab, and debridements, tissue loss progressed; after sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, HCV RNA fell to <15 IU/mL after 4 weeks and gangrene stopped spreading, but multiple amputations were required.
